What is an MLM?
• MLM = mastery learning module
• You will have:
• An at-home quiz for practice
• An in-class quiz taken through canvas.
• You are allowed one double-sided 8.5" X 11" sheet of notes (your memory 
aid). You can also use this memory aid for the graded version.
• The in-class quiz will be your only attempt to achieve mastery
• Mastery is 9/10 or 10/10
• If you achieve mastery, you get the full 5% towards your final grade.
• If you get 7/10, your grade we be normalized to mastery (i.e. 7/9)
• The purpose of MLMs are to help you master difficult concepts in 
preparation for the midterm and final exams.
• MLMs in BIOL112 have resulted in improved student performance on 
exams

• Apply your knowledge of chemistry for biology and macromolecule 
structure and function to:
• Identify or recognize the chemical properties of functional groups 
within macromolecules and the types of non -covalent interactions they 
can make
• Recognize how functional groups react during polymerization
• Recognize how directionality of macromolecules is determined
• Recognize the role(s) of macromolecules within cells
• Describe, in terms of free energy changes, the energetics of anabolic 
reactions required for the synthesis of macromolecules.
Learning Outcomes

To do this you will need to be able to:
• List the four major categories of macromolecules in cells.
• For each of the polymeric macromolecules (nucleic acids, proteins, 
carbohydrates)
• Identify or name the monomers that make up each type of 
macromolecule.
• Name the covalent bonds that link monomers to form a 
macromolecule.
• Give an example of a cellular structure or organelle where each type 
of macromolecule functions.
• Describe and explain the concepts of asymmetrical monomer polarity 
and macromolecule directionality, and why these concepts don’t apply 
to lipids.
• Identify which molecules are generally taken up from growth media versus 
molecules that are synthesized by cells.
Learning Outcomes

How and why I use clicker questions
• To take attendance
• If you answer 50% of clicker questions in a lecture, you will be 
considered present
• To promote engagement
• To help you probe your own knowledge
• To help identify and fill in knowledge gaps
• To highlight important information
• To help you begin to apply your knowledge
• To provide you with feedback 
• To provide me with feedback

How you can use clicker questions 
and pre-class quizzes to study
• Use them to test yourself after class 
• Being tested on factual knowledge soon after learning it helps you 
remember it
• Try explaining why one or more answers are correct
• Try explaining why other answers are incorrect
• Try making up your own questions using the clicker question as 
a template or model
